g.text: Kubernetes KMS v2 & k8s-kms-plugin Figure %page% of %lastpage%
Kubernetes KMS API v2 - k8s.io/kms/apis/v2 & KMS Plugin for PKCS #11
CKA_ID (Byte array) PKCS #11 Key identifier for public/private key pairs
DEK Data Encryption Key (derived by kube-apiserver from the 32-byte DEK seed)
DecryptRequest.Ciphertext holds a JWE for the aes-gcm / aes-cbc / rsa-oaep families,
and a 60-byte binary envelope (nonce | AES-GCM(DEK seed) | tag) for ml-kem.
Annotations are returned verbatim from the matching EncryptResponse: they always carry
KeyId is the hex-encoded CKA_ID of the KEK that produced the ciphertext.
After a kubernetes reboot, k8s sends both a first StatusRequest to know which key id is active.
k8s generates a new DEK seed and a corresponding EncryptionRequest in case the key id changed.
k8s sends as many DecryptRequests as their are encrypted DEK seeds in ETCD; preferably it should
not be more than 2 different DEKs at the same time. This happens during a key rotation.
Case: KEK Key Id from the k8s-kms-plugin is the same than before k8s reboot (same KEK)
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the KEK, the same than before k8s reboot>}
[For active KEK and all the old KEK Keys (As many different Key Ids) that still exist in the ETCD DB, do a DecryptRequest.]
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the KEK that encrypted it>,
unwrap the DEK seed with the remote KEK
(rsa-oaep: CKM_RSA_PKCS_OAEP unwraps the CEK inside the HSM)
read the KEM ciphertext c from the
return the same shared secret K (32 B)
re-derive the AES key from K with KMAC,
Routing is driven by the plugin's own --algorithm-family, never by the algorithm-family
annotation, so an altered annotation cannot change how a ciphertext is interpreted.
